study.title: Storylens
study.oneLiner: Event-driven LLM backend turning articles into visual summaries. Semantic prompt caching held sub-second p50 while cutting per-article model spend.

problem.context: Every article re-ran the full LLM pipeline.

decision.question: Is this worth building?
decision.chose: Semantic prompt caching in front of the LLM pipeline.
decision.why: Accepted eventual staleness in exchange for latency and cost.

steps.label: article in
steps.does: A published article arrives as an event and starts the pipeline.

steps.label: embed
steps.does: The prompt is turned into a vector so that prompts with the same meaning can be matched.

steps.label: prompt cache
steps.does: Looks for an earlier prompt with the same meaning. 70% of requests are answered here and never reach the model.
steps.fails: A cached answer can be stale. That was accepted in exchange for latency and cost.

steps.label: LLM
steps.does: Generates the visuals, summary and poll for prompts the cache has not seen.
steps.costs: Runs for roughly 3 in 10 requests instead of every one.

steps.label: visuals · summaries · polls
steps.does: Interactive visuals, a summary and a poll go back to the reader. Median response stays under one second.

study.headline: How one article becomes visuals, summaries and polls
